test_assertion_review: All ten runner tests and nine shell tests were inspected separately; none of the frozen Rust/Python assertions was removed. Runner tests use mocked command execution/prerequisites/host information and temporary dummy executable files, not actual Cargo builds: (1) scripts/tests/test_ci.py:42 asserts the complete six-command sequence, explicit host targeting, a path containing spaces, preservation of CARGO_TARGET_DIR, current artifact injection into the test child and an untouched stale parent environment. This checks handoff construction, not actual Cargo JSON or runtime environment delivery. (2) :101 injects exit 17 at each of six gate positions, asserting the same exit and no later command. (3) :120 rejects absent/invalid JSON, relative/missing executables and duplicate artifact records despite a stale environment fallback being available. (4) :137 checks subprocess argument arrays, repository cwd, env, check=True, UTF-8 text and captured stdout. (5) :150 checks the exact locked host release command without building. (6) :160 makes tool discovery fail and requires exit 1 before gates. (7) :169 removes both fixture interpreter names and requires an actionable prerequisite error. (8) :179 simulates root and permission bypass and requires rejection of both. (9) :194 injects PermissionError to accept the denial branch; despite the test name this is not native filesystem-denial evidence. (10) :202 rejects absent, empty and multiple rustc host records. Shell tests execute Bash, temporary files and real hashing/chmod tools but stub uname, rustc, gh, cargo and docker: (11) scripts/tests/test_shell_ci.py:126 checks release selection/download, checksum-success output, chmod then version execution, the exact locked host-targeted ignored-test command, and removal of the owned temporary directory. (12) :140 separately rejects missing, wrong, duplicate, malformed and unrelated checksums, absent binary and download failure; every case requires nonzero exit, no calls beyond gh and cleanup. (13) :157 verifies explicit-tag selection bypasses release view, propagates Cargo exit 31 and cleans up. (14) :164 rejects an option-like tag before any download. (15) :169 injects a Windows Rust host and requires failure without binary execution or Cargo, guarding a zero-test Linux smoke. (16) :176 checks ci.sh forwards script-tests to Python and returns exit 37; it does not exercise the python3 fallback. (17) :183 rejects a relative consumer path and a non-Linux preparation host without downstream command calls. (18) :191 checks version/config/build/load/tag ordering, no default Actions cache, the Compose command and exact unchanged smoke stdin, but the docker stub at :66 accepts arbitrary options and the assertion at :203 positively requires unsupported --no-build. It therefore encodes F1 rather than validating the real CLI handoff or containment assertions. (19) :211 checks optional cache forwarding, build exit 29 stopping before Compose run, and --push rejection before any Docker call. Existing subprocess-helper tests using ignored child fixtures remain reachable from their ordinary parent tests, while the real official-onefile test remains deliberately separate. Download-view failure, cleanup failure and real Compose argument parsing are not independently exercised by these stubs; inspected shell fail-closed branches are not substitutes for those execution records. No native/hosted/container/runtime acceptance is inferred from the reported green unit count.

blocking_findings.description: scripts/ci-container.sh:22 passes --no-build to docker compose run. That is not a supported run option: Docker's command reference at https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/compose/run/ lists --build and --pull but not --no-build; the actual Compose v2.40.3 run-command declarations at https://github.com/docker/compose/blob/v2.40.3/cmd/compose/run.go#L225 do not register it, including hidden flags and aliases. It is instead registered for create at https://github.com/docker/compose/blob/v2.40.3/cmd/compose/create.go#L79. After the preceding build succeeds, this newly added invocation is rejected during argument parsing with unknown flag: --no-build; strict-shell propagation fails the docker job before scripts/container-smoke.sh:4 can run. This is a lost required gate, not an HTTP-unreachable or test-only issue. scripts/tests/test_shell_ci.py:66 uses a permissive logging stub and :203 explicitly expects the invalid flag, explaining why the reported offline passes do not detect the defect. The failure conclusion is grounded in the real command registration, not a claimed local Docker reproduction; Docker is unavailable here and no daemon operation was performed.
reachability_proof: .github/workflows/ci.yml:48 creates the Ubuntu docker job, whose step at line 55 calls bash scripts/ci-container.sh with cache arguments.

scripts/ci-container.sh:22 then passes the unsupported run option before the service name, so Compose rejects it before the /bin/sh override and scripts/container-smoke.sh input at line 23 can execute.
Consequently scripts/container-smoke.sh:4's non-root checks, line 7's tmpfs checks and line 19's executable probe are unreachable on this otherwise valid invocation.
blocking_findings.minimal_fix_direction: Use the supported Compose run interface for the already-loaded local image, retaining --pull never, --no-deps, --rm, -T, the shell entrypoint override and unchanged smoke input; remove the unsupported flag rather than weakening or skipping the gate. Correct the test expectation and guard the real CLI contract instead of having a permissive stub bless arbitrary options. Do not change deployment defaults or invoke the production installer.
blocking_findings.verification: First check the intended runner's actual docker compose version/run help and ensure the repaired command contains only supported options; update and run the lightweight orchestration regression tests, including command failure propagation. When separately authorized on native Linux with Docker, run bash scripts/ci-container.sh and require the loaded local image plus the final container-smoke success message, not merely a green stub. Record that the shell override, original non-root user/tmpfs configuration and nonzero assertion failures are preserved without publication or installer boot. Native Docker and hosted execution remain pending until those records exist.
